title: Bostrom's Simulation Argument
rootClaim: It is statistically overwhelming that our current reality is a computer simulation engineered by a post-human technological civilization.

branches.text: Bostrom's Trilemma dictates that unless civilizations go extinct early or refuse simulation research, simulated ancestors exponentially outnumber real humans.

children.text: Computational Feasibility: A post-human civilization possessing planet-scale computing power could run billions of high-fidelity ancestor simulations easily.
Energy and Thermodynamics Limits: Simulating quantum mechanics for 10^80 particles in an entire universe requires more energy than exists in the physical world.
Procedural rendering: The simulation only needs to compute fine-grained quantum events when observed by a conscious entity (like rendering in video games).
Principle of Indifference: Since simulated minds vastly outnumber biological minds across the multiverse, any random observer should assign a high prior to being simulated.
Self-Indication Assumption Bias: Using anthropic reasoning to infer simulation status introduces subtle probabilistic paradoxes in reference class selection.

branches.text: The Simulation Hypothesis is epistemically unstable, scientifically unprovable, and morally problematic.

children.text: Infinite Regress Problem: If our universe is simulated, the host universe could also be simulated, leading to an infinite regress with decaying computational capacity.
Regress Termination: The root universe at the top of the stack must be physical, but that does not reduce the statistical dominance of lower-tier simulations.
Falsifiability & Occam's Razor: Proposing unseen post-human simulators introduces immense extra entity assumptions over accepting our physical observations directly.
Simulated Glitches & Constraints: Pixellation of spacetime at Planck scale and cosmic ray energy cutoffs could represent hardware limitations of the underlying computer.

definitions.description: The proposition that at least one of three claims is true: (1) humanity goes extinct before post-humanity, (2) post-humans don't run simulations, or (3) we live in a simulation.
The rule in probability theory that in the absence of relevant evidence, equal probabilities should be assigned to all possibilities.
In graphics and simulation theory, computing details only when and where an observer is looking rather than simulating the full environment constantly.
The group of observers to which an individual compares themselves when calculating anthropic probabilities.
